# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kawata_2019_gefitinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kawata_2019_gefitinib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-019-03788-4> (open access, PMC6458983)

Kawata 2019 measured plasma gefitinib in a prospective Japanese cohort with a
nested case-control study of interstitial lung disease (ILD; NCT00252759). The
population PK model (Results, Table 2; Online Resource) is a one-compartment
model with first-order absorption and a lag time (NONMEM ADVAN2 TRANS2), fitted
with the FO method to log-transformed concentrations. Clearance CL/F depends on
serum alpha1-acid glycoprotein (AGP), body weight, age >= 65 years, concomitant
CYP3A4 inducers and whether the sample was drawn at the time of ILD diagnosis;
volume V/F depends on AGP and body weight.

The paper's second analysis, a multivariate logistic regression of ILD
occurrence on exposure quartiles and clinical risk factors (Online Resource
Supplementary Table 1, Figure 3), is not packaged: only odds ratios are
printed (no intercept), and the quartile boundaries are given only for the
third quartile, so the regression cannot be reconstructed as a predictive
model.

# Population

336 Japanese patients with advanced or recurrent non-small-cell lung cancer
who had received at least one prior chemotherapy regimen took gefitinib 250 mg
once daily at 50 centres between November 2003 and February 2006 (Table 1).
Mean age was 64.8 years (range 37-87; 180 aged >= 65), mean weight 55.5 kg
(33-100), 152 were women, and mean serum AGP was 121.3 mg/dL (31-327). 23
patients took a CYP3A4 inducer. 51 patients developed ILD. The model was fitted
to 1891 concentrations: 943 after the first dose, 911 at steady state (days
10-15) and 37 drawn at the time of ILD development in 27 of the ILD patients.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Kawata_2019_gefitinib")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 1-cmt, first-order absorption, lag time | ADVAN2 TRANS2 | Results; Online Resource |
| CL/F equation | `theta1*(AGP/121)^theta2*theta3^AGE65*theta4^IND*(WGT/55.5)^theta5*theta6^PERI` | Table 2 |
| V/F equation | `theta7*(AGP/121)^theta8*(WGT/55.5)^theta9` | Table 2 |
| `lcl` | log(28.6 L/h) | Table 2, theta1 |
| `e_aag_cl` | -0.502 | Table 2, theta2 |
| `e_age_ge65_cl` | 0.759 | Table 2, theta3 |
| `e_cyp3a4_ind_cl` | 1.82 | Table 2, theta4 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.503 | Table 2, theta5 |
| `e_dis_ild_acute_cl` | 0.743 | Table 2, theta6 |
| `lvc` | log(1540 L) | Table 2, theta7 |
| `e_aag_vc` | -0.447 | Table 2, theta8 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.766 | Table 2, theta9 |
| `lka` | log(0.819 1/h) | Table 2, theta10 |
| `ltlag` | log(0.863 h) | Table 2, theta11 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalka`, `etaltlag` | log(1 + CV^2) = 0.218, 0.138, 2.09, 0.0679 | Table 2 omega rows (49.3%, 38.5%, 266%, 26.5%) |
| `expSd` | sqrt(log(1 + 0.327^2)) = 0.319 | Table 2 sigma (32.7%); additive error on log scale per Online Resource |
| AGP reference 121 mg/dL = 1.21 g/L | `ref_aag` | Table 2 equations; unit conversion to the canonical `AAG` column |
| Weight reference 55.5 kg | `ref_wt` | Table 2 equations (cohort mean, Table 1) |

# Virtual cohort

Covariates are drawn to match Table 1. Values outside the observed ranges are
redrawn, not clamped, so the distributions are not piled up at the limits. AGP
is drawn log-normally with the Table 1 mean and SD and converted to g/L.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190214)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190214)
n_sub <- 200

draw_in_range <- function(n, draw, lo, hi) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- draw(n)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

agp_sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (52.4 / 121.3)^2))
agp_meanlog <- log(121.3) - agp_sdlog^2 / 2

cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = draw_in_range(n_sub, function(n) rnorm(n, 55.5, 11.0), 33, 100),
  AGE = draw_in_range(n_sub, function(n) rnorm(n, 64.8, 9.1), 37, 87),
  AGP_mgdl = draw_in_range(n_sub, function(n) rlnorm(n, agp_meanlog, agp_sdlog), 31, 327),
  CONMED_CYP3A4_IND = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 23 / 336),
  DIS_ILD_ACUTE = 0
) |>
  mutate(
    AAG = AGP_mgdl / 100,
    AGE_GE65 = as.integer(AGE >= 65)
  )

summary(select(cohort, WT, AGE, AGP_mgdl, AGE_GE65, CONMED_CYP3A4_IND))
```

# Simulation

Two dosing scenarios are simulated for every virtual patient: the first 250 mg
dose (observed 0-24 h) and a 250 mg dose at true steady state (`ss = 1`,
observed over one 24-h interval). This mirrors the paper's first-dose and
steady-state exposures, which were model-predicted from the empirical Bayes
estimates.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Kawata_2019_gefitinib")
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.1), seq(4.25, 24, by = 0.25))))

make_events <- function(cov, ss_flag, label) {
  dose <- cov |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = 250, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = 24, ss = ss_flag)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(cov, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = 0, ss = 0L)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(treatment = label)
}

ev_sd <- make_events(cohort, 0L, "First dose")
ev_ss <- make_events(cohort, 1L, "Steady state")

keep_cols <- c("id", "treatment")
sim <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_sd, keep = keep_cols, returnType = "data.frame")),
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_ss, keep = keep_cols, returnType = "data.frame"))
)
```

```{r profiles, fig.cap = "Simulated gefitinib concentrations after the first 250 mg dose and over one dosing interval at steady state (median and 5th-95th percentiles of 200 virtual patients)."}
sim |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Gefitinib (ng/mL)")
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r nca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_df <- bind_rows(ev_sd, ev_ss) |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, ctrough = TRUE)
nca_res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
```

## Comparison against the published exposures

Figure 1 of Kawata 2019 prints the median model-predicted Cmax, AUC0-24 and
Cmin for patients without ILD (n = 285 after the first dose, n = 277 at steady
state). They are the reference here because the virtual cohort carries no
ILD-related difference; the 51 ILD patients had higher exposure (medians 214
ng/mL, 3974 ng.h/mL and 141 ng/mL after the first dose). Cmin is the
concentration at the end of the 24-h interval (`ctrough`).

The steady-state exposures do not depend on the absorption rate and should
match closely. The first-dose Cmax and AUC0-24 are expected to come out
somewhat lower than the published medians. The published values are empirical
Bayes predictions, and the ka random effect has 57% shrinkage (Table 2), so the
published ka values cluster near the typical 0.819 1/h. The simulation instead
draws ka from the full population distribution (CV 266%), and the slow
absorbers in that tail lower the first-dose Cmax and AUC0-24.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast, ~ctrough,
  "First dose", 157, 2992, 107,
  "Steady state", 434, 8830, 292
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_df,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL", ctrough = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Median simulated vs published (Figure 1, patients without ILD) gefitinib exposure after 250 mg once daily. * marks rows differing by more than 20%."
)
```

```{r nca-gate}
sim_med <- nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "ctrough")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
ref_long <- published |>
  pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref")
gate <- inner_join(sim_med, ref_long, by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - ref) / ref)
gate
# A 200-subject cohort median moves by up to about 25% between covariate and
# eta draws (steady-state Ctrough is the noisiest), so the gate is on the
# centre of the six differences plus a loose envelope. A mis-transcribed
# clearance, volume, dose or unit shifts all six by far more than either.
stopifnot(
  nrow(gate) == 6,
  abs(median(gate$pct_diff)) < 12,
  all(abs(gate$pct_diff) < 40)
)
```

## Typical-value checks

For the reference patient (AGP 121 mg/dL, 55.5 kg, < 65 years, no CYP3A4
inducer, not at ILD development) the steady-state AUC over one interval must
equal Dose / (CL/F) = 250 mg / 28.6 L/h = 8741 ng.h/mL. At the time of ILD
development CL/F is multiplied by 0.743, so the steady-state AUC rises by
1 / 0.743 = 1.346; Figure 2 of the paper reports median AUC0-24 of 10141 and
13643 ng.h/mL in the same 19 patients outside and at ILD development, a ratio
of 1.345.

```{r typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
ref_pat <- tibble(
  id = 1:2, WT = 55.5, AAG = 1.21, AGE_GE65 = 0, CONMED_CYP3A4_IND = 0,
  DIS_ILD_ACUTE = c(0, 1)
)
ev_typ <- make_events(ref_pat, 1L, "Steady state")
sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, keep = "id", returnType = "data.frame"))

nca_typ <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(filter(sim_typ, !is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | id),
  PKNCAdose(filter(ev_typ, evid == 1), amt ~ time | id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE)
)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast")

auc_ref <- nca_typ$PPORRES[nca_typ$id == 1]
auc_ild <- nca_typ$PPORRES[nca_typ$id == 2]
c(auc_ref = auc_ref, expected = 250 / 28.6 * 1000, ild_ratio = auc_ild / auc_ref, fig2_ratio = 13643 / 10141)
# Same drawn parameters on both sides; the difference is trapezoid error only.
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_ref / (250 / 28.6 * 1000) - 1) < 0.005,
  abs((auc_ild / auc_ref) / (1 / 0.743) - 1) < 0.005,
  abs((auc_ild / auc_ref) / (13643 / 10141) - 1) < 0.01
)
```

# Covariate effects

```{r covariates, fig.cap = "Typical CL/F and V/F across the observed AGP range for 40, 55.5 and 80 kg patients (age < 65 years, no CYP3A4 inducer)."}
agp_grid <- tidyr::crossing(AGP_mgdl = seq(31, 327, length.out = 60), WT = c(40, 55.5, 80)) |>
  mutate(
    cl = 28.6 * (AGP_mgdl / 121)^-0.502 * (WT / 55.5)^0.503,
    vc = 1540 * (AGP_mgdl / 121)^-0.447 * (WT / 55.5)^0.766
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(cl, vc), names_to = "param", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(param = recode(param, cl = "CL/F (L/h)", vc = "V/F (L)"))
ggplot(agp_grid, aes(AGP_mgdl, value, colour = factor(WT))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Serum AGP (mg/dL)", y = NULL, colour = "Weight (kg)")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV and residual scale.** Table 2 prints each random-effect row as
  "omega (%)" and the residual row as "sigma (%)" without saying how the
  percentage was computed. They are read as log-normal CVs, so each variance
  is log(1 + CV^2) and the residual SD on the log scale is
  sqrt(log(1 + 0.327^2)). The other common convention, 100 times the SD of eta,
  would give variances about 10%, 7% and 3% larger for CL/F, V/F and tlag,
  and a ka variance of 7.08 instead of 2.09. The difference matters only for
  ka. Under that reading the simulated first-dose median Cmax and AUC0-24 fall
  roughly 25% below the published Figure 1 medians, against roughly 13% below
  under the CV reading (median over several cohort draws). The comparison
  favours the CV reading, though shrinkage keeps it from being decisive. Steady-state exposure is unaffected by either reading.
* **AGP units.** The paper reports AGP in mg/dL; the packaged model takes the
  canonical `AAG` column in g/L (AGP mg/dL / 100) with the reference 1.21 g/L,
  which is the paper's 121 mg/dL.
* **ILD period covariate.** The paper's `PERI` flag is packaged as
  `DIS_ILD_ACUTE`: 1 for records at the time of ILD development, 0 otherwise.
  It is time-varying within a patient. The authors note that AGP was not
  measured at ILD development and suggest the CL/F reduction may reflect an
  ILD-induced AGP rise.
* **CYP3A4 inducers.** The paper does not name the inducers pooled into
  `IND = 1`.
* **Steady state.** The paper predicted steady-state exposure "assuming steady
  state at 144 h after the first dosing"; the vignette uses a true steady-state
  dose (`ss = 1`). For a typical half-life of 37 h, 144 h is about 3.9
  half-lives, so the paper's steady-state exposures could be a few percent
  lower than true steady state.
* **Virtual cohort.** Table 1 gives only means, SDs and ranges, so weight and
  age are drawn as normal and AGP as log-normal within the observed ranges,
  independently of one another. No patient is at ILD development in the
  cohort.
* **Comparison reference.** The published Figure 1 medians are empirical Bayes
  predictions in the observed patients, while the simulation draws new
  patients from the population distribution; agreement of the medians, not
  of the spread, is the check.
* **Logistic regression of ILD risk.** Not packaged (see Model and source).
